1.explanation: The file src/languages/cpp.js defines the C++ language grammar, including its list of keywords and how they are matched. The missing highlight for “switch” indicates that it was removed or mis-classified in the keyword definition in v10.7.0. Restoring or adjusting its entry in this file will fix the syntax highlighter for C++ switch statements.
1.bug_scenario: Starting in highlight.js v10.7.0 the “switch” keyword in C++ blocks is no longer being colored as a control-flow keyword, while other statements (if, while, for) continue to highlight correctly. In the provided before/after screenshots you can see that “switch” stays plain text (grey) instead of getting the keyword color (green) as it did in v10.6.0 and v11.x.

2.explanation: The C++ language definition lives in src/languages/cpp.js and is responsible for registering the full set of C++ keywords and control-statement modes (including switch). It typically extends or delegates to the base C grammar in src/languages/c.js, which itself declares the core control keywords (if, else, for, while, switch, etc.). Any regression in how ‘switch’ is listed, parsed, or inherited between c.js and cpp.js would cause switch to stop being highlighted. To restore correct highlighting you’ll need to inspect and correct the keyword lists or mode definitions in these two files so that ‘switch’ is again treated as a keyword in C++ code.
2.bug_scenario: The user reports that as of highlight.js 10.7.0 (and later), C++ “switch” statements are no longer recognized as keywords—so in a snippet with if/ switch/ while/ for, “if”, “while” and “for” all get the correct keyword styling but “switch” is rendered as plain text. In earlier versions (≤ 10.6.0) “switch” was properly highlighted. The supplied before/after screenshots clearly show “switch” dropping out of the keyword color.
